text:
james: Heads-up — noticed odd sparsity in prefix cache hit-rate on the new heatmap. Large customers show spikes of near-zero hit-rate for long-context routes since yesterday after kernel update. Link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc123/prefix-hitrate-sparsity?orgId=1
lina: :eyes: can you paste the customer IDs or route names? is this across all models or just long-context Llama2 variants?
james: Mostly /generate-chat-long and model variants 'llama2-70b-long', 'redwood-rlhf-long' — per-model panels show hit-rate collapse for top 3 tenants. Token-saved numbers also dropped ~60k tokens/hr for each tenant.
omar: I ran a profile on the serving node that got the kernel bump. CPU ingress ok, but kernel selected different matmul kernels for int8 paths. Could that change KV cache key hashing timing? :thinking: 
ciara: KV is agnostic to matmul kernels, but batching heuristics changed — scheduler fold now allows larger micro-batches which might perturb prefix alignment and key derivation if we used sequence-bound keying.
james: Here's a quick query I ran against the telemetry index:
```
SELECT model, route, tenant, avg(hit_rate) as hr, sum(tokens_saved) as ts
FROM prefix_cache_metrics
WHERE ts >= now()-24h
GROUP BY model, route, tenant
ORDER BY hr ASC
LIMIT 50;
```
Result: a cluster of tenants with hr < 0.02 on /generate-chat-long, but other routes unaffected.
lina: Can we check warmup coverage? maybe prefetch agent misfired after the kernel rollout. @ops-bot — did any rollout happen at ~3948160000?
ops-bot: deploy-notification: kernel-defaults update rolled out to zone prod-us-east-1 at 3948162100 by infra-team. No prefetch changes in that deploy. :information_source: 
omar: I can repro locally by toggling scheduler fold on. When fold enabled, prefix-key windowing shifts by micro-batch size. That will change normalized key fingerprints for sequences with padding.
ciara: If fingerprint changes, cache miss explosion makes sense. We should surface per-tenant fingerprint-variance metric in the dashboard. I'll add a panel.
james: Actionable: (1) roll kernel-defaults back on a canary tenant (ops?) (2) add fingerprint-variance and per-tenant warmup coverage panels (ciara) (3) diag script to recompute keys for affected tenants and see if hits return (omar)
lina: I can run rollback on one canary. Which tenant should we pick? recommend 'acme-enterprise-3' — it's already throttled but representative.
omar: I'll prepare the diag script. expected runtime ~3m per tenant. posting skeleton:
```
# diag-key-check.py
for t in tenants:
  sample = get_recent_prefixes(t, limit=1000)
  keys = [derive_key(p, folding=enabled) for p in sample]
  diff = key_similarity_before_after(keys)
  print(t, diff)
```
ciara: Nice. I'll add alert rule: if any tenant's hit-rate drops by >10pp in 5m and token_saved delta >5k/min, page eng-runtime on-call.
james: Thanks team. Keep updates in this thread. I'll attach the initial heatmap screenshot in comments and pin the grafana link. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: perf-alert: prefix-hitrate-anomaly detected for tenants: acme-enterprise-3, brightside-inc, sandbox-42 at 3948201300
lina: starting rollback on acme-enterprise-3 now — will update when complete.
james: good. once rollback finishes, check tokens_saved and hr panels. If both recover, schedule a follow-up to change key derivation to be stable vs micro-batch folding.
